position_outside: UN/LOCODE places Huelva on the city (37.25, -6.95), north of the port areas mapped here. The cargo quays are downstream, on the Odiel and on the Palos de la Frontera bank.

properties.source: Derived: the convex hull of this port's terminals and way 835855938 from OpenStreetMap, grown by 500 m
properties.note: OpenStreetMap maps no port limits for Huelva. These are the hull of the outer port at Muelle Sur and the inner port area on the Odiel, grown by 500 m. They take in the river and the land between, so they are rougher than the legal limits.

properties.name: Puerto de Huelva
properties.note: The outer port on the Palos de la Frontera bank, mapped as an area named Puerto de Huelva and tagged landuse=industrial, with the Muelle Sur point inside it. Cargo is from the port authority: Muelle Sur is its container and general cargo quay, and Yilport Huelva runs the 58,000 m² container terminal on it, with 240 reefer plugs (Fruit Attraction, 2024). The area is larger than that terminal, so no operator is given.

properties.name: Muelle Reina Sofía
properties.note: The refinery's liquid bulk jetty, mapped as a line tagged man_made=pier, so this area is that line grown by 50 m, enough for a tanker alongside. The port authority's statistics list its berths, Reina Sofía C, W, E and 4º atraque, as CEPSA's liquid bulk jetties; CEPSA has traded as Moeve since 2024.
